title: Repeats and road signs
summary: Follow repeat marks, D.C., D.S. and Fine through a piece, and read a metronome mark.

hook.text: A song’s chorus comes back again and again. Printing it every time would waste paper, so music has shortcuts. Press play. This music is only two [[bar|bars]] long on the page. How many [[bar|bars]] do you hear, and what does the cursor do?

explore.text: Press play and watch the cursor jump. The page has three [[bar|bars]], but you hear five. Play the clip again, then play the tune yourself on the keyboard, jumping back wherever the cursor does.
explore.goal: Play the clip, then play the tune on the keyboard, jumping back where the cursor does.

cards.text: [[repeat-marks|Repeat marks]] are a double [[bar-line|bar line]] with two dots. Where the dots face left, go back and play again from the start sign, whose dots face right. With no start sign, go back to the beginning. Press play and follow the cursor.

[[da-capo|Da capo]] (*D.C.*) says go back to the beginning. [[dal-segno|Dal segno]] (*D.S.*) says go back to the sign: a curly S with a slash and two dots. [[fine|Fine]] is where the piece ends, and [[al-fine|al fine]] means play on until Fine.

A [[metronome-mark|metronome mark]] gives the speed as a number. ♩ = 80 means 80 beats every minute, and the note shows which note counts as one beat. It often sits beside a speed word. This tune is marked *Andante*, ♩ = 80.

alternative.text: Think of a road trip. Repeat marks are a roundabout: go round again. *D.C. al Fine* says drive back to the start, then stop at the finish line: [[fine|Fine]]. A [[metronome-mark|metronome mark]] is the speed limit sign. Press play and watch where the cursor goes.

questions.prompt: Three tunes are written on the page. One comes round twice. Which page matches what you hear?
questions.hint: Count the tunes as they go by. Which one do you hear two times in a row?

options.reason: This page repeats the first [[bar|bar]], so the opening tune would come twice at the start. In the clip, the tune that comes round twice is the second one.
This page repeats the last [[bar|bar]], so the closing tune would come twice at the end. In the clip, the second tune is the one that is repeated.

questions.prompt: Which sign sends you back to the very beginning?
questions.hint: Think of the words: da capo means from the head, the top of the piece.

options.reason: [[fine|Fine]] marks where the piece ends, not where to go back to. Going back to the very beginning is *D.C.*, [[da-capo|da capo]].
That curly sign is the *segno*. *D.S.* sends you back to it. Going back to the very beginning is *D.C.*, [[da-capo|da capo]].

On to the end: the piece is over

questions.hint: A metronome counts beats. Think of a clock ticking: what does the number count each minute?

options.reason: A [[metronome-mark|metronome mark]] is about speed, not repeats. The number counts beats, and repeats are shown by dots on a bar line.
The number does not set how long you play. It counts how many beats fit into one minute, which is 60 seconds.

questions.prompt: The page has 3 [[bar|bars]] and ends with *D.C. al Fine*. How many [[bar|bars]] do you hear?
questions.hint: Count the tunes as they go by. Where does the music jump back to, and where does it stop?

options.reason: Three is only what is written. *D.C.* sends you back to the beginning, so you play more than the page holds.
Six would mean playing the whole piece twice. *Al fine* says to stop at [[fine|Fine]], which is the end of [[bar|bar]] 2, so [[bar|bar]] 3 is not played again.

questions.hint: A mark of 60 is one beat a second. Tap along: is the clip about that speed, or much quicker?

options.reason: ♩ = 60 is one beat a second, which is slow. The clip runs at more than two beats a second, so it needs the bigger number.

questions.prompt: Which sign shows where to stop after *D.C. al Fine*?
questions.hint: It is a word that means the end.

options.reason: *D.C.* sends you back to the beginning. It does not say where to stop: that is [[fine|Fine]].
Dots on a bar line are [[repeat-marks|repeat marks]]: play a section again. The stopping place is marked [[fine|Fine]].

questions.prompt: One piece is marked ♩ = 60 and another ♩ = 120. Which is faster?
questions.hint: The number counts beats in one minute. Which piece fits more beats into that minute?

options.reason: A smaller number means fewer beats a minute, so the music is slower. ♩ = 60 is half as fast as ♩ = 120.
The numbers are different, so the speeds are too. ♩ = 120 packs twice as many beats into each minute as ♩ = 60.

points: Repeat marks are a double [[bar-line|bar line]] with dots. Go back to the start sign, or to the beginning if there is none, and play the section again.
Da capo (*D.C.*) means go back to the beginning. Dal segno (*D.S.*) means go back to the sign.
Fine is where the piece ends. Al fine means play on until Fine.
A metronome mark such as ♩ = 80 gives the speed: 80 beats every minute.
